title: Call-stack quarantine and structured output contracts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: When an incoming request triggers multi-tool chaining (tool A -> tool B -> model -> tool C) we currently have two related hazards: 1) result injection attacks or accidental semantic contamination where tool outputs re-enter the language model as untrusted text and cause recursion or hallucinated state, and 2) inconsistent streaming semantics and structured-output contracts when partial tool results are emitted while the chain is still active. Goal: Add a lightweight call-stack quarantine and a structured-output contract layer that preserves streaming behavior for clients while preventing recursive injection and providing backwards-compatible fallbacks for legacy clients.
acceptance_criteria: Call-stack quarantine ledger that separates tool-originated tokens from user/system tokens and prevents automatic re-injection into model prompt unless explicitly authorized
A streaming-compatible framing protocol so partial tool outputs can be proxied to clients without exposing raw tokens to the model input layer
A structured-output contract (JSON schema + version) that tools and models negotiate; older clients can opt into a compatibility mode that receives flattened text
End-to-end tests showing recursion detection fires within 50ms for pathological chains (depth > 6) and prevents end-to-end infinite loops
Performance overhead <= 3% p99 latency for typical request shape (single tool call, streaming) when the quarantine is enabled
API docs and spec published with sample SDK usage for explicit injection authorization and backward compatibility toggles
Security review completed and sign-off on threat model for tool-result provenance
design_notes: High-level approach: 1) Maintain a call-stack ledger for each request containing compact provenance tokens (tool_id, op_id, timestamp, declarative trust flag). Ledger entries are opaque at runtime and are not concatenated into the model prompt. 2) Provide an explicit 'inject' API that takes a ledger reference plus a transformation policy (passthrough, sanitize, summarize) to allow controlled re-introduction of tool results into the model context. 3) For streaming, implement a dual-path proxy: partial tool output is streamed to the client and simultaneously checkpointed to a protected buffer referenced by ledger ID rather than inline prompt insertion. 4) Add a structured-output contract registry with schema versioning; runtime validates tool outputs against declared schema when provided and returns structured fragments as events over the streaming channel. 5) Backwards-compatibility: if client requests compatibility-mode, runtime will serialize structured fragments into text using a deterministic flattener and annotate provenance headers.
implementation_plan: Design ledger proto and minimal fields: tool_id, op_id, origin_hash, trust_level, created_at
Add protected buffer store and ledger lifecycle TTL (default 5m) and eviction semantics
Implement streaming proxy with event framing: event types = {tool_partial, tool_complete, structured_fragment, model_token, error}
Build 'inject' API surface for SDKs and internal callers with explicit auth checks
Integrate schema registry checks on tool outputs and runtime validation errors with graceful fallback to compatibility mode
Add recursion detector: maintain per-request depth counter + op fingerprinting and soft/hard bailouts
Load tests and p99 latency evaluation against baseline; optimize by inlining small ledgers and batching ledger writes
